title: S3a evidence reuse from cancelled or failed workers: partial results become evidence objects with provenance worker_partial, routed to the replacement worker (P27)
spec:
orchestrator/evidence.py: add provenance value worker_partial to PROVENANCE (trust_class LOCAL_USER, trust field untrusted stays as for non-repo provenance, scan applied as for any evidence). orchestrator/worker_control.py: after cancel builds the partial result, and in a new hook worker_control.preserve_partial(task) that daemon.reconcile_dead calls for a dead worker with a dirty worktree, create evidence objects in the goal's evidence pool (evidence.make with source_type worker_partial, location the task id plus the worktree head sha, content = the partial facts rendered as compact lines: files changed with diff stat, commits with subjects, tests run and their result lines, error tail, files inspected; commit = worktree head sha; freshness by the existing hash mechanism). Replacement routing: orchestrator/context_router.py treats worker_partial evidence whose location task shares the same goal and overlaps the current task's scope (write or read) as high relevance (never HIDE) with a cap of [context_router].partial_max_tokens (default 800, dated comment); orchestrator/spawn.py renders those items under a packet section prior_worker (after evidence) with the source task id and the head sha, so the new worker can check out or diff it instead of rediscovering; the section is empty when nothing applies. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/16-evidence-reuse.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.
acceptance: tests/test_worker_control.py::test_cancel_and_preserve_partial_create_evidence_objects (pool contains the facts with commit sha; no prompt or transcript text)

spec_review_risks.issue: Spec adds worker_partial to PROVENANCE and calls evidence.make(source_type=worker_partial,...), but SOURCE_TYPES (evidence.py:16-20) is a separate tuple that does not contain worker_partial and make() validates source_type against it independently (evidence.py:77-78, raise ValueError). As written this call raises ValueError: invalid source_type. Spec conflates provenance and source_type.

_trust_class (evidence.py:42-43) is a hardcoded dict {'repo':'TRUSTED_REPO','memory':'LOCAL_USER'}.get(provenance,'EXTERNAL') — any provenance not explicitly listed falls to EXTERNAL. Adding worker_partial only to the PROVENANCE tuple does not give it LOCAL_USER; the dict itself needs a new explicit entry, which the spec never names as an insertion point. Also plan.md:39's stated contract ties LOCAL_USER specifically to user-authored 'memory' provenance, not daemon-observed git/test artifacts — pairing worker_partial with LOCAL_USER is a new, undocumented trust semantic.

Rendering of the prior_worker packet section in spawn.py is not stated to be gated by [context_router].mode (currently 'shadow' per pool.toml:357, which today only 'computes and logs the routed packet without changing what the model sees'). House rule requires shadow-first: a new adaptive path must not change what a worker sees until mode is active. The spec doesn't specify that prior_worker rendering stays inert while mode=shadow, risking a live behavior change under a flag that's supposed to be inert.

reconcile_dead's dirty-worktree branch (daemon.py:380-384) has no idempotency guard; tick() calls it every ~30s for any task still status=running with a dead pid (daemon.py:1655-1663), and any exception in the inserted preserve_partial() is swallowed by tick()'s except/continue, leaving status=running so preserve_partial re-runs every tick. EvidencePool.add() dedupes by exact content hash, but drifting content (changing log tails) across ticks would accumulate distinct evidence rows rather than truly dedupe — a state-never-decreases risk the spec doesn't address.

'Scope overlap (write or read)' between the dead worker's task and the current task has no existing data model to compute from: read_scope (context_router.py:55, spawn.py:584-585) is synthesized ephemerally per-packet for the requesting task only and is never persisted or retrievable for a different (dead) task. The spec assumes a comparison that requires new plumbing to capture and store the dead task's read footprint, which isn't scoped.

'freshness by the existing hash mechanism' is inaccurate: fresh() (evidence.py:109-110) is a plain commit==head_sha string check gated to only source_type in (source_chunk, test_result); any other source_type is always considered fresh. For the new evidence to actually go stale on a newer head_sha, fresh() (and context_router's duplicate check at context_router.py:83-85) must be extended to include the new source_type — this is an unstated required change, not reuse of existing behavior.

Spec's 'existing tests' table claims tests/test_worker_control.py is missing, but the file exists today (103 lines, class WorkerControl(unittest.TestCase) with 5 existing tests). The new acceptance test must be added as a method inside that existing class/file, not a new file — minor but could mislead the executor into scaffolding a duplicate test module.
